messages:
amanda: Heads-up — running into a pain point with the Python SDK + tracing. When we use OpenTelemetry context the trace headers don't get forwarded to downstream services (so our traces break at the Redwood call).

josh: Hmm, can you paste a minimal repro? async or sync? which HTTP lib?

amanda: async, using httpx AsyncClient via the async client. Example: 
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from opentelemetry import trace
client = AsyncClient(api_key=..., base_url=... )
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)
async with tracer.start_as_current_span("test-call"):
    resp = await client.generate("hello")
```
We expect the OTEL context to be propagated (so the outbound HTTP request carries traceparent), but the logs show no trace headers.

priya: Oh I ran into this too last week. I think the SDK does its own short-circuit transport that doesn't use httpx's event hooks, so context manager isn't applied. I have a small stack trace: "RuntimeError: No active span" when the client tries to read current span inside its generated request path.

josh: That sounds like the client code executes outside the instrumented context. Is redwood AsyncClient using any threadpool or background task?

amanda: Looks like the internal send happens inside a coroutine, but we still have context in other calls. I traced it to the transport wrapper in client/_transport.py where it builds headers. It reads os.environ['REDWOOD_X_REQUEST_ID'] fallback and doesn't consult OpenTelemetry.

tarun: We should support two things: 1) automatic propagation of OTEL headers when a span exists, 2) expose a middleware hook for adding custom headers like request-id. Both are small changes.

emily: Typing note: while adding hooks, can we also improve type defs for streaming responses? Right now mypy complains: "generator returned Any" when streaming tokens. The signatures should be AsyncIterator[str] or AsyncGenerator[Token, None].

priya: Agreed. Also parity request: sync client should mirror async behavior for tracing. Right now sync uses requests + prepared requests and *does* include trace headers when using requests instrumentation, but async path is broken.

amanda: Quick workaround for anyone hitting this: manually inject trace headers using opentelemetry's TraceContextTextMapPropagator. Example:
```py
from opentelemetry.propagators.textmap import DictGetter, inject
headers = {}
inject(headers)
resp = await client.generate(..., extra_headers=headers)
```
But we shouldn't force users to do this.

josh: Good interim. For long-term: proposal for SDK API additions:
- Client.add_middleware(callable) that receives (request, next) and can mutate headers
- Automatic propagation toggle: propagate_tracing=True|False on client init
- Expose request_id generation hook or allow passing request_id from context manager

tarun: Implementation notes: if we add middleware, ensure it supports sync and async middlewares (callables that may be awaitable). Also keep middleware order predictable. We'll need to add typing stubs: Protocols for MiddlewareSync and MiddlewareAsync.

emily: For OTEL, we should avoid depending on opentelemetry APIs at import time. Lazy import or optional integration is better (extra dependency). Suggest: package redwood[otel] to pull opentelemetry. If not installed, we no-op.

amanda: Also request IDs — we should pick a standard header name (X-Redwood-Request-Id?), and if user provides a header with their own request id, preserve it. If not, generate one and log it. Ops wants correlation automatically.

priya: I opened a quick PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/412 (WIP) — it adds a middleware hook and an opt-in propagate_tracing param. Needs tests for context propagation and for httpx AsyncClient path.

sdk-ci-bot: Build queued for PR #412 — running unit tests.

josh: Thanks — can you add a test that uses opentelemetry test tracer to assert the outgoing request has traceparent header? We can stub the transport to capture headers.

priya: Yep, will add. Also will update types: StreamingResponse -> AsyncIterator[str] and add TypedDict for Request/Response shapes so middleware can be typed.

tarun: Small UX ask: sample app in docs showing both sync+async tracing setup and an example with OpenTelemetry Collector/OTLP exporter config. That helps customers onboard.

emily: Agreed. Also add note in migration guide: if you rely on auto headers today, pin to previous version until we release the fix.

amanda: Thanks team — keep me posted. If someone wants to pair on the async test tomorrow LMK. :+1:

josh: I'll pair with you 10am PT.

sdk-ci-bot: PR #412 tests passed on linux-3.10, flake8 warnings on typing stubs.

priya: Fixed flake8, pushed update. Will link RFC for middleware shape once tests green.

amanda: Awesome — closing loop here, feel free to ping me if we need more QA on traces or logs.
